reviewer_summary.question: Why must a selected word become a new input, and how can saved data at each layer reduce the repeated work?
reviewer_summary.takeaway: Choosing blue uses is’s finished result; processing blue produces a new result while reusing the earlier pieces’ unchanged keys and values.

findings.problem: Holding a half-input number through later operands/product/parts loses the connection to choosing the next word.

resolution.note: Replace disappearing operation cards with one persistent two-branch diagram. Keep both operands, reached results, target amount and completed prior source amount visible; move current focus while the diagram remains in place.

findings.problem: Fractional sharing parts differ from counting integer practice parts.

resolution.note: Name the result one and a quarter relative sharing parts and explain that recipe parts can be fractional amounts.

findings.problem: Three silent new values compete with the prior layer values.

resolution.note: Name each second-layer key/value result and explicitly bind it to layer two, with longer inspection and row focus.

findings.problem: The separate practice allocation can compete with the actual allocation in memory.

resolution.note: Retain the short prerequisite example because earlier readers could not connect parts to fractions without it. Clearly leave the practice case; the new persistent diagram parks actual operands/amounts so they need not be held against the practice numbers. Fresh recheck remains required.

findings.problem: Presentation instructions compete with learning why layer two has different data.

resolution.note: Narration now explains only separate second-layer inputs and source preparation; the compact display and old/new labels explain themselves visually.
